verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to break this and it broke in six independent places, only one of which the candidate anticipated.

WHAT SURVIVES. The candidate's factual claims about the physics side are true as stated, and I verified each. torque_slope measured 5.87027377274637e-22 J/turn against an analytic 2*pi*C/L prediction of 5.87027377274637e-22, ratio 1.0, all five rod gates PASS (outputs/chromatin_rod.json). Lk drift 4.440892098500626e-16 across eight refine/coarsen ops (same file, refine_chain). The K562 ladder and the 0.0211 bar are real (outputs/orphan/nexus_txn.json). And the claim I most expected to be the kill — "the cell model has no genomic coordinates" — is FALSE: I counted directly and 16380 of 16492 gene records carry both chrom and tss, exactly as the candidate said. Credit where due; the candidate counted honestly.

WHAT BREAKS.

1. THE QUANTITY IS AN INPUT, NOT AN OUTPUT. This is the kill. chromatin_supercoil.py imposes sigma at line 204 as a four-element tuple and reports the resulting ensemble. It does not infer sigma from anything. So "one float per gene" has no source. Searching for any per-locus supercoiling assay (GapR-seq, psoralen, TMP-seq) returns nothing — the only "supercoil" strings in cell_complete.json are GO annotation text.

2. THE BLOCK IS RANK 1, BY THE REPO'S OWN ARITHMETIC. The candidate proposes F6 = [torque_pNnm, sigma_domain] and in the same breath calls them "equivalently" the same thing. They are: torque = slope * dLk with slope fixed at ratio 1.0 to 2*pi*C/L, and dLk = sigma * Lk0 exactly (-6.857142857142857 / 342.85714285714283 = -0.02). At fixed L the two columns are one column under an affine map. With the only available sigma constant, variance is 0 and the measured gain is exactly 0.0000 against a 0.0211 bar.

3. THE MECHANISM IS SIGNED AND THE SIGN IS ABSENT. Twin-domain is entirely about the asymmetry: negative behind, positive ahead. "Behind" and "ahead" require strand. I checked all 16492 records — `strand` is present in none, and so are `start`, `end`, and any gene-length field. nexus_txn.py itself gives this away: PROM = 2000 with a symmetric tss +/- PROM window, which is what you write when you do not have strand. The coupling's whole content cannot be assigned a direction.

4. IT NEEDS A REDUCTION MEASURED TO FAIL, ON THIS EXACT SYSTEM. Treating a 2-10 kb window around each TSS as carrying a per-gene torque is a locality assumption. Locality by norm was tested on the twistable rod and FAILS: quantity 1.0 vs threshold 0.25, with frac = 1.0 and norm_in = 1.0 at R = 10, 20, 30, 50, 70 AND 100 (outputs/physics_reduce_rod.json). There is no radius at which the rod truncates. That is physically correct — twist redistributes over the whole topological domain — which is why the candidate reaches for "sigma of the topological domain containing the promoter" instead. But no domain assignment exists (0/16492 records), so the escape hatch is closed too. Separately, finite-amplitude linearity on the rod is NOT TESTABLE (deviation 0.8555143567608874 vs threshold 0.001), so nothing licenses superposing per-gene torque contributions.

5. TWIN-DOMAIN IS A DRIVEN STEADY STATE AND THE REPO HAS ONLY EQUILIBRIUM MC. The sigma that matters is the balance of Lk injected by elongation against Lk removed by topoisomerase. grep returns topoisomerase in exactly three places (chromatin_supercoil.py:42, :251; chromatin_rod.py:3) and all three are prose. No relaxation rate, no injection rate, no model. The repo's own capability note says the MC gives "equilibrium configurations between events, NOT trajectories through them". The quantity being proposed is not the quantity the code computes.

6. THE SCORING HARNESS CANNOT BE RUN. The candidate's "scored on the identical 5 x 70/30 held-out gene splits already in that file" is false twice. The splits are not stored — they are regenerated by RandomState(0) shuffling `genes = sorted(set(dc.feature_ID) & set(info))`, which needs dc. And dc is rnadecay/AvgKdegs.csv, the TARGET variable, which a filesystem-wide search does not find, along with k562_atac.bed.gz, _abcfeat.json and lambert_tf_symbols.json. nexus_txn.json stores only summary rows (r, r2, within_2x, n) — no per-gene predictions, no residuals, no split indices. The 0.0211 bar is measured and real; nothing in this container can be measured against it.

ON THE "CONSERVATIVE LOWER BOUND" DEFENCE. The candidate's most sophisticated move is to pre-concede the writhe-partition failure (frac_hi 0.9656831950986892 vs 0.70-0.75) and reframe it as a signed, conservative bias. The direction is right and the repo's own reading says so. But chromatin_resolution.json tried to explain that overshoot and returned three false gates (falls, bending_costlier, reaches_literature) with the conclusion that the overshoot "lives in the model" — and that file recorded only ONE of its three predeclared bead counts, so its reported change is a row compared with itself. An unexplained bias of unmeasured magnitude is an uncalibrated bias, not a bound. Nothing measures whether it is monotone across genes, which is what a tree model would need for it to be harmless.

I also note the candidate correctly fences off the melting/SIDD step as unbuildable. That fence is honest and I do not need it — the coupling fails well upstream of denaturation.
verdicts.refutation_attempted: The strongest argument AGAINST this coupling — the one I would lead with — is that the quantity it proposes to carry is a free parameter dressed as a measurement. sigma enters chromatin_supercoil.py as a hardcoded four-element tuple at line 204 and leaves as the same number; torque is its exact affine image (slope ratio 1.0, dLk = sigma*Lk0 to the digit). So F6 is one column, not two, and there is no per-gene value to put in it: 0 of 16492 gene records carry sigma, domain, tad, or strand. The coupling does not survive. The strongest defence available to it is that per-gene sigma could be DERIVED from twin-domain physics rather than measured — polymerase flux injects Lk, topoisomerase removes it, and the steady state gives you a per-gene number. That defence fails twice over: the repo has no topoisomerase model at all (three prose mentions, no rate), and more damagingly the derivation is circular — twin-domain sigma at a promoter is a function of that gene's elongation flux, which is the prediction target k_syn. Fitting it would reproduce exactly the failure mode nexus_txn.py declined by name in its own docstring, where a free IDR beta was refused because it "would absorb error and inflate R2 without adding biology", and k_on/k_off/k_ini were refused as unidentifiable from bulk steady-state rates. Per-gene sigma is unidentifiable from bulk steady-state rates for the same reason. The one genuine concession I make against my own refutation: the candidate's coordinate claim is TRUE (16380/16492 carry chrom and tss, counted directly), so the usual "no genomic coordinates" objection does not apply here and I did not use it.
verdicts.what_would_unblock: Five things, in order of how hard they bind. (1) A per-locus superhelical density measurement — GapR-seq, psoralen/TMP-seq, or equivalent — mapped to hg38 coordinates. Absent from this container; without it sigma is a constant and the column has zero variance. This is the one that matters, and no amount of compute substitutes for it. (2) `strand` and a gene-end coordinate in outputs/orphan/cell_complete.json (currently 0 of 16492 records have either). Twin-domain is a signed mechanism; without strand you cannot say which side of the TSS is over-wound, and nexus_txn.py's symmetric PROM = 2000 window confirms nothing downstream knows the direction. (3) The four missing nexus_txn inputs restored to the scratch dir, above all rnadecay/AvgKdegs.csv, which carries the TARGET k_syn = RPKM * k_deg. Alternatively, persist per-gene predictions and split indices into outputs/orphan/nexus_txn.json so a new column can be scored against the recorded 0.0211 bar without re-deriving the splits from data that is gone. (4) A topoisomerase relaxation rate and a polymerase Lk-injection rate, so the twin-domain steady state is computed rather than imposed — and a demonstration that the resulting per-gene sigma is identifiable WITHOUT using the transcription rate it is meant to predict, since otherwise the column is circular. (5) A domain-scale locality result to replace the failed one: locality by norm on the rod is 1.0 against a 0.25 threshold at every radius out to R=100, so some measured statement about over what contour length torque can be treated as a per-gene scalar is needed. Note that even with all five, the timescale license is thin at domain scale — tau_rouse 0.021851328219019688 s at 100 kb against the 0.030303030303030304 s polymerase interval is only 1.387x, and 1 Mb fails by 72x. WHAT IS BUILDABLE TODAY AND IS NOT THIS COUPLING: the closed-form torque(sigma, L) table from chromatin_rod.py is validated at ratio 1.0 and costs nothing. It is a correct piece of physics with no gene to attach it to. Shipping it as a feature column would be shipping a constant.

verdicts.reasoning:
GENOMIC COORDINATES ARE NOT THE WEAK POINT HERE. I checked: rouse_gate.py lines 175-187 reads chrom/chromStart/chromEnd/startTSS from outputs/orphan/invivo/crispr_egpairs.tsv and builds (chrom, element_midpoint, TSS) triples per pair. The destination subsystem does hold real bp coordinates. That half of the candidate survives. Everything else does not.

1. THE MINIMAL FORM IS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY NULL. The candidate offers a fallback: "one extra column sigma_shared_domain per element-gene pair", grounded on "4904 measured K562 contact domains (hic_gate.json)". That column exists. hic_gate.py computes F[i,5] = both loci inside one contact domain and names it "same_domain" in FEATNAMES. It ran against those exact 4904 domains and returned coverage 0.0796, net -0.0031 with se 0.0030 (z = -1.055), sign_consistent false. The candidate's central claim -- "a contact channel with no representation at all in the current models" -- is contradicted by a recorded run in the file the candidate itself cites. The genuinely-new part is only the sigma weighting.

2. THE SIGMA WEIGHTING HAS NO ARGUMENT. Both proposed representations need sigma at a genomic locus. That quantity does not exist in this container in any form. The feature compendium's 14 columns carry no torsional variable; invivo/ holds ChIP, DNase, H3K27ac and ABC BEDs only; a whole-filesystem search for supercoiling tracks returns nothing but the MC simulation's own output. The only in-repo signals that could stand in for transcription-generated supercoiling are polr2a_enh and procap_enh -- and those are already columns 4 and 5 of the base arm that scores 0.6076. The learner is XGBoost at max_depth 4, which is invariant to monotone transforms of a feature, so a sigma proxy built from them is arithmetically incapable of adding information. The new channel has no input.

3. THE SOURCE MEASUREMENT'S OWN GATE FAILED, AND ITS LOG FORBIDS EXACTLY THIS. chromatin_supercoil.json records writhe_fraction = false, frac_hi 0.9657 against a predeclared, untuned external target of 0.70-0.75. The candidate cites zero_sigma_flat and C0_control passing as licence, but those two gates only establish that the buckling is torsional in origin -- they say nothing about its magnitude, and magnitude is the entire content of an Rg multiplier. The quantity being imported is the one the failed gate governs: Rg falls because the chain writhes, and it writhes 1.29-1.38x more than measured DNA. Direction of the bias is known (compaction overstated); size is not measured. chromatin_resolution.py then tested the predeclared excuse and rejected it ("MY EXPLANATION WAS WRONG... the overshoot lives in the model"), and both logs close with the same instruction: "Nothing should be layered on top until this is understood." The candidate is precisely that layering.

4. THE Rg CURVE'S OWN BASELINE IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE. The candidate's headline is "Rg falls from 94.91182072048208 nm at sigma 0 to 51.551413649341804 nm at sigma -0.06". outputs/chromatin_supercoil.json records the sigma=0 row as Rg 94.9 nm / Wr -0.011 / E 65.7 kT. The stdout capture written at the identical mtime, under an identical header, records that same row as Rg 80.7 nm / Wr -0.002 / E 63.8 kT, while the three stressed rows agree to the digit. No rg_sd is recorded at any sigma. Propagated through the candidate's own P ~ <R^2>^(-3/2), the claimed contact enhancement is 6.24x on one artifact and 3.84x on the other -- a 1.63x spread in the imported quantity, from one run. That is not a calibration a multiplier can be built on.

5. SCALE. The candidate declares 10 kb to ~1 Mb. The largest supercoiled system this repo has ever equilibrated is 4000 bp. The destination pairs have a median span of 370,392 bp, 82.6% exceed 100 kb, and only 2.4% fall at or below 10 kb. The Rg(sigma) headline system is 3600 bp -- 0.72 of a SINGLE 5 kb bead of the rouse_gate.py chain it is proposed to modify. There is no measured Rg(sigma, L) scaling law, and the one length probe on record (2000 -> 4000 bp) measured only the writhe partition, not Rg scaling. Extrapolating 92.6x is exactly the interpolation the ground rules forbid.

6. COST, if you tried to close the scale gap by measurement. From the two in-file MC timing points (N=61 at 0.1244 s/sweep, N=121 at 0.7591 s/sweep, exponent N^2.641), one configuration at the median 370,392 bp span at the supercoil run's own 50 bp/bead resolution is 689 core-days at N^2.64 and 3,020 core-days at the code's own stated N^3 -- for ONE sigma at ONE length, before any per-pair work. The BD/AMR alternative is priced too: the cost model's fine-window law is measured and strictly linear (100 kb = 10.0 days on 4 cores), so a 370 kb resolved window is 37 days on 4 cores per pair, ~1,048 core-years over the 10,331-pair ladder. And it would not help anyway: the finest AMR level is a 200 bp bead = 68.0 nm, 7.6-13.6x too coarse to host the 5-9 nm plectonemic superhelix that is the whole mechanism.

7. THE CEILING ARGUMENT THE CANDIDATE MISREADS. The candidate cites hic_over_ctcf = -0.0076 as evidence that competing ingredients are closed, clearing the field for torsion. It is the opposite. It says that REAL, MEASURED, cell-type-matched Hi-C contacts -- the ground truth of what actually touches what, torsional plectonemes included, since Hi-C sees every contact regardless of its physical cause -- add negative value on top of counting CTCF sites. Any torsional contact channel that is real is already inside the measured Hi-C map, and the measured Hi-C map is worth -0.0076. verdicts.reasoning:
Four independent blockers, any one of which is sufficient.

(1) CATEGORY ERROR IN THE MECHANISM. The candidate asserts "the quantity that must clear tau is ... initiation frequency". It is not. Both files that carry the constant label it as elongation: colab/chromatin_timescale.py:73 "s between polymerase steps, 33 bp/s" and colab/chromatin_cost_model.py:65 "POL_RATE = 33.0 # bp/s. RNA Pol II elongation, ~2 kb/min". 30.3 ms is how often ONE polymerase perturbs the chain as it adds a base; k_syn is a synthesis flux in RPKM/h. Swapping one for the other is a substitution of physical quantities, not a refinement of resolution. The 303.030303030303 s the candidate cites as evidence the constant "reappears" in the cost model is 10000 bp / 33 bp/s -- it reappears precisely BECAUSE it is an elongation speed applied to a contour length.

(2) NO HEADROOM, AND THE WRONG SIGN. Even granting the substitution, the arithmetic kills it. Flipping the tightest holding verdict (100 kb Rouse, margin 1.38678x) needs >45.76 events/s at one locus; flipping 10 kb needs >4576.4 events/s. Both exceed the 33/s elongation clock. And a per-gene initiation interval is necessarily LONGER than the per-base elongation interval at the same locus, because each initiation is followed by thousands of elongation steps on the same template. The cost model already runs 10x looser than 30.3 ms (0.30303 s/event at 10 bp/event). So the per-gene column can only push verdicts toward HOLDS. The deliverable is a table in which no row can differ in verdict from the single global number it replaces. That is not "a per-locus verdict", it is the same verdict re-tabulated 7631 times.

(3) NEITHER COLUMN OF THE PROPOSED TABLE EXISTS ON DISK. The representation is {gene, chrom, tss, k_syn, event_interval_s, N in bp, tau_Rouse, tau_Zimm, verdict}. chrom and tss DO exist -- 16380 of 16492 genes in cell_complete.json carry both, so the "cell model has no genomic coordinates" weak point is REFUTED. But (a) k_syn per gene is gone: colab/txn_rate_model.py:50 reads it from SP/rnadecay/AvgKdegs.csv, which is absent from this container; only summary statistics survived into txn_rate_model.json (median 3.4152 RPKM/h, 4.5754 decades, n_pairs 88695) and 7631 is a COUNT in txn_rate_accuracy.json, not a table. (b) "domain contour N in bp" per gene does not exist either -- cell_complete.json has a TSS but no gene end or length (all 23 per-gene keys enumerated), there is no GTF/BED/GENCODE anywhere on the box, and loops3d gives 767 single anchor coordinates rather than domain spans. Since N is the ONLY axis on which the repo's Rouse/Zimm verdict actually varies, its absence removes the one column that could have made rows differ.

(4) THE INPUT'S PER-GENE RANKING FAILS ITS OWN RECORDED CONTROL. The honesty flag concedes the absolute conversion is not measured and falls back to "what is measured is the ranking". The repo measured exactly that ranking and it did not survive: rate_ground_truth.json puts derived k_syn against direct TT-seq K562 at r = 0.36055946235014674, Spearman 0.34699068010258566, on n_shared 7462, and records cell_specific = false because the cross-cell-line control (derived HEK293T against measured K562) scores 0.3717 -- HIGHER than K562 against itself at 0.3606. Plain RPKM alone reaches 0.2252. So the per-gene ordering the deliverable is built on is indistinguishable from a different cell line's ordering. The fallback position of the candidate is the exact quantity the repo already refuted.

(5) THE STATED "WHY NOW" IS FALSE ON ITS OWN SOURCE. The candidate claims "warm-start validity is precisely what a shortened event interval decides". The cost model's log says the opposite in the sentence that introduces iters_warm = 5: "A polymerase step perturbs a few hundred base pairs and the previous state is an excellent initial guess, so a WARM restart should need far fewer". Warm-start quality is set by the SPATIAL perturbation between events (bp/event) and its amplitude, not by wall-clock waiting. In an overdamped quasi-static scheme the between-event state is the equilibrium state; waiting longer makes the quasi-static assumption better, never worse, and does not change the initial guess. So the coupling does not touch the softest number in the cost model.

No reduced form rescues it. The one honest place k_syn belongs is the EVENT-COUNT axis of the cost model (transcription events per unit time genome-wide -> number of solves), not the timescale-separation axis -- but that route needs the same missing per-gene table plus the RPKM-to-molecules normalisation the repo explicitly says it does not have (rate_ground_truth.py:323, ec_capacity.py:40). It also does not need locality (measured to FAIL, 1.0 vs threshold 0.25 in physics_reduce.json) or finite-amplitude linearity (NOT TESTABLE on the rod), so those known failures are not what stops it -- the mechanism and the missing data are.

Cost is not what blocks this, so I priced it first and set it aside. Acetyl is the mark the candidate wants and it needs a 40 A region: 2.54e6 histone marks on chr22 x 3.105 s = 91.3 core-days (recorded in chromatin_mark_cost.json), which is 8.6 h on 256 cores; genome-wide is 91.3 x 122 = 1.11e4 core-days = 30.5 core-years, or 43.5 days on 256 cores. The physics side of this candidate is real, cheap and correctly cited. Three independent things block it anyway.

FIRST, the energy budget, which is the hardest constraint because it survives granting everything else. The acetyl mark's total mechanical work on the whole particle is 0.5769154796125926 model units = 2.120334209705245 kcal/mol at the repo's own calibrated spring scale. nexus converts ddG_bind to occupancy through a two-state equilibrium anchored at dG_bind_wt = 9.0 kcal/mol. The chain's own recorded demo agrees: ddg_bind 6.0 kcal/mol moves activity to 0.992. The strongest case FOR the coupling: strain energy is the wrong bound. A reader's ddG_bind does not come from extracting the nucleosome's stored strain; it comes from geometric complementarity, and sub-Angstrom shifts at a real interface routinely cost kcal/mol. Peak |u| is 1.6537113960546053 A for acetyl-K and 3.385064802412569 A for phospho-S (chromatin_mark_cost.json) -- huge on that scale. bind_ddg itself reaches r 0.45 and hotspot AUC 0.791 from geometric descriptors, so geometry-to-affinity is demonstrably learnable. It partly survives, and it does not rescue the candidate. Those peak displacements are AT the marked atom, at the most-buried lysine of 114 (200 neighbours within 10 A against a minimum of 28). Acetyl's per-atom strain falls 623x from bond shell 0 (0.07536415472159878) to shell 3 (1.2099887757582228e-04), 54 bonds carry 90% of it, and no interface bond appears in the top 1000 (iface_top1000 = 0.0). So the deformation is confined to a few bond shells around a buried site, and the field at any docking surface is unmeasured -- chromatin_mark_cost judges convergence on a fixed 10 A evaluation set (EVAL_R = 10.0), and the only measurement that speaks to the far field, the Green-column truncation, shows norm_in 0.16385337941520997 with max |u| of 9.339378730585489 A sitting OUTSIDE every radius tested. And the biology the steelman gestures at -- a bromodomain reading an acetyl-lysine -- is chemical recognition of the added group, which needs none of the Green's-function machinery and is a different coupling from the one proposed. The steelman therefore establishes that the mechanical bound is not the only conceivable route, not that this route works.

It has no consumer: nothing downstream can read a 3N vector, and the only place it could enter (nexus_txn L4) holds integer graph degrees and cannot be re-run here for want of its four input files.

I decomposed the cost model rather than trusting its headline: 5.0e-8 s per bead-step on 4 cores, 3.46692e10 fine steps per 200 bp bead, so 1733.46 s per fine bead (27.09 s on 256 cores). The candidate's own headline is therefore right and fatal: 7631 genes at 10 kb is 76.31 Mb of resolved window = 6.614e8 s = 20.96 years on 4 cores, 119.6 days on 256. One day on 256 cores buys 3190 fine beads = 638 kb total, i.e. 63 intervals at 10 kb or 319 at 2 kb. The proposed list is 121x over budget at 10 kb. Domain size being free does not help, because the candidate is not asking for a bigger domain — it is asking for more resolved base pairs, which is the one thing the model prices linearly.

(1) A persistent fine window is a locality assumption, and locality by norm is the repo's one clean rejection on this exact model class: on the twistable rod, physics_reduce_rod.json records quantity 1.0 against threshold 0.25, with 28 of 28 beads carrying 90% of the norm at every radius from 10 to 100. Nothing licenses treating a bounded region as the only place the response lives. (2) The Lk = 4.44e-16 result the candidate leans on was measured on uniform whole-chain refinement (48 -> 768 -> 48, every operation changing all beads). No mixed-resolution state was ever built, so the standing fine/coarse boundary that a persistent window creates is untested — and the cost model's own log flags a leak at a moving refinement boundary as THE engineering risk precisely because it drifts rather than blows up. THE LEDGER IS FINE. THE SIGNAL IS NOT. Lk bookkeeping is the single best-tested object in the 4d chromatin line: drift 4.440892098500626e-16 across eight refine/coarsen operations (chromatin_rod.json), and the cost model had flagged exactly this as the architectural risk that "would drift and look like physics". The candidate is right that this licenses the topology edit. But the coupling does not transport Lk -- it transports TORQUE, and in this codebase torque is C*2*pi*Tw/L (colab/chromatin_rod.py:214-218), a function of TWIST. Getting from the ledger's dLk to torque requires the Tw/Wr partition, and that partition is a predeclared gate that FAILED at 0.9656831950986892 against 0.70-0.75.

THE ARITHMETIC OF THE FAILURE. Twist share measured = 0.03431680490131084 against literature 0.25-0.30, so torque is 7.285x to 8.742x under-estimated. Concretely, using only repo constants (C = 4.066e-28 J m, RISE = 0.34e-9 m/bp, omega0 = 0.5984 rad/bp -> 10.5 bp/turn): one 1 kb fork event injects 95.238 turns; in a 100 kb domain 2*pi*C/L = 0.07514 pN nm per turn, so one event is 7.156 pN nm if all dLk stayed as twist, 1.789-2.147 pN nm at the literature partition, and 0.2456 pN nm at this model's partition. A topoisomerase-demand signal that reports a quarter of a pN nm where the literature partition gives two is not a demand signal.

THE "KNOWN BIAS DIRECTION" DEFENCE DOES NOT SURVIVE. The candidate concedes the bias and argues it is conservative. Two things kill that. First, this is a threshold phenomenon -- the claim is that torque "eventually stalls the fork" -- and an 8x under-estimate of a threshold-crossing quantity does not fail conservatively, it fails to fire. Second, the bias is not a constant that can be divided out: across the repo's own probe rows the partition runs from 0.9010902300590073 (C = 55 nm) to 0.9693489686729915 (sigma -0.04), i.e. the twist share runs 0.0989 to 0.0307, a 3.223x spread in the correction factor, and it moves with C, with excluded volume and with sigma. chromatin_resolution.json tested and rejected the predeclared resolution explanation ("MY EXPLANATION WAS WRONG"), and chromatin_partition_probes.json concludes the residual is entirely in E_bend'(Wr) with none of the tested knobs closing the gap. There is no scalar rescale available.

THE SCHEME IS ALSO ILLEGAL AT THE PROPOSED SCALE. The candidate specifies 100 kb to 1 Mb domains, quasi-statically event-stepped. chromatin_timescale.json extrapolates tau_Rouse to 0.021851328219019688 s at 100 kb and 2.1851328219019686 s at 1 Mb against a 0.030303030303030304 s event interval -- separations of 1.3868 and 0.013868 against the reducer's own licensing threshold of 1000 (physics_reduce.json). And the file names the failing channel by name: quasi-static stepping is valid for the LOCAL torsional response and "INVALID for long-range chain conformation -- writhe redistribution, plectoneme motion". Writhe redistribution is precisely the operation the dLk-to-torque conversion needs. THE COST NUMBERS ARE QUOTED FROM THE WRONG COLUMN. The candidate quotes warm 1016816.4 s (11.8 days) for one chr1 fork. So the applicable column is cold: 13015249.92 s = 150.6 days on 4 cores for a single chr1 fork, and 2017331199.9999998 s = 64.0 years (364.8 days on 256 cores) for full S phase. THE QUANTITY DOES NOT EXIST ON THE RECEIVING SIDE. This is the known weak point and it is worse than stated. The candidate names two receivers. THREE INPUTS ARE ABSENT FROM THIS CONTAINER, NOT JUST ONE. WHAT WOULD SURVIVE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A COUPLING. A hand-placed fork on a 2-4 kb rod, tracking dLk exactly and reporting the Lk ledger with NO torque claim, is buildable today and cheap -- chromatin_rod.py and chromatin_supercoil.py need no external data, and the largest such run on record is 4000 bp / 121 beads / 400 sweeps at 303.65 s. The candidate's own fallback ("the ledger, its cost, and the torque it implies for a fork placed by hand") is the from-side alone, and its torque term is exactly the part the failed gate invalidates. There is no reduced form that still crosses the subsystem boundary, which is why this is BLOCKED and not BUILD REDUCED.

verdicts.reasoning:
I set out to refute this and it fails on three independent grounds, any one of which is sufficient.

1. THE SOURCE QUANTITY DOES NOT EXIST. The certificate is a function tau(L), and L is taken from "loop-anchor span". I reproduced the candidate's counts exactly -- 163 genes, 119 over 100 kb, 5 over 1 Mb -- so the arithmetic is honest. But the repo's own provenance audit (/home/user/cell/UPDATES.md) records that the loops3d loader "stored only the partner anchor's bin start, discarding the gene's own anchor and the resolution." A gene with two stored anchors therefore has the far ends of TWO DIFFERENT loops, not the two ends of one domain. max-minus-min across them is the distance between two unrelated loop partners. It is not a contour length, and no arithmetic downstream can make it one. The same audit classes loops3d MEASURED-DEAD ("2 KO-KO pairs out of 979,300"), and it is GM12878 while the cell model is K562 throughout. Coverage compounds this: 163/16,492 = 0.988% of genes could receive a flag at all, and 99.01% get nothing. The 5 kb gcd I measured across all anchor positions is the resolution the loader is recorded as having thrown away.

2. THE CONSUMER DOES NOT EXIST. The stated mechanism is that treating chromatin state as a static per-locus number "is licensed only if the polymer re-equilibrates between biological events." That premise is false for this cell model. Its chromatin state is a ChromHMM label read off ENCODE K562 ChIP-seq at TSS+-2kb -- epigenetics.py calls it "a LABELING of measured data." A population-averaged ChIP-seq annotation is not the output of a quasi-static stepper; it is not licensed or unlicensed by whether one polymer relaxes in 30 ms. There is no event stepper on the cell-model side whose validity a certificate could certify. Nor is there a clock to compare against: the 0.0303 s interval comes from POL_RATE = 33.0 bp/s defined inside chromatin_cost_model.py, and grep finds no time constant of that scale anywhere in the cell model, whose own dynamic layer runs at FBA doubling times of ~24 h. The certificate would cross the boundary and land on nothing.

3. THE MARGIN IS SMALLER THAN THE ADMITTED ERROR. The candidate concedes the extrapolation caveat but then proposes to emit precisely the two things the caveat forbids: a boolean and a margin ratio. Both are functions of the prefactor, and chromatin_timescale.py states in-line that "the prefactor is not trustworthy -- only the exponent argument is." The numbers show why that matters: the Rouse crossing sits at 117,762 bp, the margin at 100 kb is 1.387x, and the calibration carries +/-11.7% from tr(K^+) alone before any prefactor question. With a median observed span of 185,000 bp, the flip is on the wrong side of the median, so the per-gene boolean is decided by exactly the factor the file disowns. What survives the caveat is the qualitative statement "the licence flips with contour length" -- which chromatin_cost_model.py:170 has already absorbed ("the quasi-static separation FAILS above ~100 kb") and used to justify the AMR ladder. That work is done, inside 4D chromatin, without needing the cell model.

WHAT I COULD NOT USE AGAINST IT, in fairness. The candidate is right that this needs no solve, so the reductions measured to fail -- locality by norm (physics_reduce.json, quantity 1.0 vs threshold 0.25) and finite-amplitude linearity (physics_reduce_rod.json, NOT TESTABLE) -- do not bind here. Cost genuinely is negligible. The coupling does not die of expense; it dies of having no measured quantity on either end.

So the chemistry covering 76.9% of the receiving annotation would, on the repo's own reasoning, behave like the single worst-behaved row — and it was never actually run.

2. THE PREMISE. The mechanism claims amplitude 'is a property of the chemistry and of the nucleosome, not of the genomic locus'. That is the load-bearing claim, and it is measured at n = 1 site per class. most_buried() (mark_cost.py lines 202-213) picks the argmax of neighbour count within 10 A — deliberately the extremum of the burial distribution, chosen so the three marks are comparable TO EACH OTHER, not so any is representative. The repo records no |u|max variance across sites, so 'constant' is asserted, not measured. Worse for the one row that joins: acetyl was measured at the most BURIED lysine, while H3K27ac sits on the H3 N-terminal tail — the least buried, most solvent-exposed part of the particle. The single joinable number is sampled at the opposite end of the distribution from the mark it would be joined to. And 'phospho-S' was measured on a THREONINE OG1 (the file's own log: 'phospho on THR OG1 atom 6868'), so even the row labels do not match what was run. The upstream '31M near-identical nucleosomes' justification is a docstring assertion in greens.py and twolevel.py with no variance measurement behind it.

3. THE CONSUMER. Grant the join anyway. The candidate's own gate (1) concedes the column is mechanical amplitude only and must not be read as accessibility — correctly, since interface strain loads at 0.0070 (5mC) and 0.0000 (acetyl) against 1.5136 for the shuffled control. But accessibility is the only channel by which the cell model turns chromatin into transcription: cellos.py's epi command consumes a categorical ChromHMM label and epigenetics.py (b) applies a repressive-state GATE. There is no field that takes an Angstrom. Grep confirms zero existing wiring — the chromatin physics modules are imported only by each other, epigenetics only by cellos. So the table can be attached and nothing reads it.

4. The second constant is worse. The 'region radius' is a cost parameter for computing the field with a boundary-fixed local solve. The cell model performs no elastic solves, so that column has no meaning on the receiving side even in principle — and for 5mC and unscreened phospho it does not exist (None).

Two things I want to credit, because rejecting sloppily is as bad as accepting sloppily. First, every |u|max and near_err the candidate quotes is verbatim correct against chromatin_mark_cost.json; I checked all five rows and all ten radii. Second, the known weak point I was told to probe — whether the cell model holds genomic coordinates — is NOT the problem here: 16,380/16,492 genes carry chrom+tss. The candidate also correctly avoids the two measured-to-fail reductions: it needs neither locality-by-norm (physics_reduce.json FAILS at 1.0 vs 0.25) nor finite-amplitude linearity (NOT TESTABLE on the rod), because |u|max comes from the exact full-structure solve. It is a well-constructed proposal that is blocked by data and by an unmeasured premise, not by physics or by arithmetic.
verdicts.refutation_attempted:
Strongest argument AGAINST the coupling: the table is keyed on a chemistry axis the receiver does not use. 76.9% of genes (12,595/16,380) are annotated only by lysine-methylation marks that have no row, and 3 of 5 rows have no track in this container to join to at all.

The candidate's best defence, which I steelmanned: 'fine — drop to a 1-row table, acetyl-K joined to h3k27ac, which still reaches 8,955 genes (54.7%), and ship it as a precomputed annotation.' Does my attack survive that retreat? Yes, on three independent counts, any one of which is sufficient:
(a) the number is n=1, measured at the most-buried lysine by construction (most_buried, mark_cost.py line 202), while H3K27ac is a histone-tail lysine — so the value is sampled at the opposite extreme of the burial distribution from the mark being annotated, and no variance measurement exists to bound the error;
(b) the value is ambiguous by 1.7413x (1.6537 unscreened vs 0.9497 screened) purely from a salt assumption the source file forbids quoting as a fact about chromatin;
(c) there is no consumer — the accessibility bridge is refuted at interface ratio 0.0070/0.0000 vs 1.5136 shuffled, and cellos.py/epigenetics.py expose only a categorical label and a repressive gate, with no slot for an Angstrom.
A one-row table with an unmeasured constancy premise, 1.74x modelling ambiguity, measured at the wrong structural site, feeding nothing, is not a reduced coupling — it is a decoration. The attack survives.

I also tried and FAILED to refute it on two fronts, and record that honestly: cost (25.43 s to rebuild, join runs in minutes — cost is not the binder) and missing coordinates (16,380/16,492 genes have chrom+tss, so the usual weak point is not weak here).
verdicts.what_would_unblock: Four things, in order of how much each buys. (1) RUN THE MISSING CHEMISTRY. Histone lysine methylation is named in chromatin_mark_cost.py's own docstring taxonomy but omitted from MARKS[]; it is the chemistry behind 4 of the receiver's 6 tracks and 12,595/16,380 genes (76.9%). Adding it costs one more Green column — 88.98566166559856 ms on top of an existing factorisation (chromatin_greens.json). This is the single highest-value missing measurement in the whole candidate and it is nearly free. Note the predeclared expectation should be pessimistic: it is +1-charged and sterically 5mC-like, and 5mC is the row that never converges. (2) MEASURE THE PREMISE. Re-run |u|max at n >= 20 sites per mark class sampled ACROSS the burial distribution — explicitly including exposed H3/H4 tail lysines, not most_buried() alone — and report the spread. If |u|max varies less than ~1.7x across sites (the salt ambiguity already baked into the acetyl row), 'constant table' is earned; if it varies more, the coupling is dead as a table and would need a per-locus field, which the cost model rules out. (3) SUPPLY THE ABSENT TRACKS. A K562 WGBS/5mC track and a phospho (e.g. H3S10ph) ChIP track would make 3 of the 5 existing rows joinable; without them those rows are unjoinable regardless of how good the physics is. (4) FIND OR REFUTE A CONSUMER. The accessibility bridge is measured dead (interface 0.0070/0.0000 vs shuffled 1.5136), so some OTHER measured channel from Angstrom-scale displacement to a transcription-relevant quantity must be established before any mechanical column has a destination. Until (4) exists, (1)-(3) only produce a better-populated table that still nothing reads.

verdicts.reasoning:
The candidate is two claims welded together, and they have opposite fates.

THE CERTIFICATE SURVIVES. "Do not compute the conformational ensemble at 25 kb" is measured three independent ways and I could not break it. chromatin_spheres.json: spheres 0.09543917217994027 vs phantom 0.09968891787260052 — restoring the single largest missing piece of physics changes nothing, and the run is live (71% of overlaps removed, 0.03930345052083334 -> 0.011229036458333334). rouse_gate.json: ROUSE adds +0.0031250 over base and +0.0049331 over CTCF, against CTCF's own +0.0556239 — real but an order of magnitude redundant with counting. contact_decompose.json: even MEASURED Hi-C is hic_over_ctcf -0.007619271491370094. Priced from chromatin_spheres.json's own log figure of ~1 GPU-day/region at 4 Mb, the refusal cancels 8 GPU-days on the recorded chr22 span and 775 GPU-days genome-wide (3.1e9/4e6 regions). That half is BUILD NOW.

THE PAYLOAD DOES NOT SURVIVE. Three independent refutations, any one sufficient.

(1) The consumer is provably blind to it. The candidate says the float is "used as the distance-decay null in the cell model's contact / enhancer-gene scoring". That scoring is crosscell_eg.py, whose FEATNAMES[0] is "log_dist" with X[i,0] = np.log10(max(abs(t-em),1)), and which additionally carries dist_rank and dist_excess. The model is xgboost. P(s) ~ s^a means log P = a*log s — an affine rescaling of feature 0. Gradient-boosted trees split on thresholds and produce identical partitions under any strictly monotone transform of a single feature. The exponent therefore adds exactly zero, for every value of a. It is not weakly informative; it is unidentifiable in the named consumer.

(2) The repo already ran the best possible version of this and recorded NO. residual_contact.json is precisely the proposed object — obs_over_exp and contact_residual at resolution_bp 25000. Crucially its docstring says "Expected is fitted from the data itself, per distance bin, so no external expected-model is assumed." The repo deliberately chose an EMPIRICAL per-bin expected over a fitted power law, and that choice strictly dominates: a per-bin expected reproduces any decay shape exactly, while s^a is a one-parameter approximation to it. So the candidate proposes a strictly weaker version of something already measured. Result of the stronger version: +0.0010306 pooled, +0.0042193 MRR, dmrr_sign_p 0.26014579678753663, and the full contact block landing BELOW baseline at 0.5548209174986355. Recorded verdict: "NO -- ... buy CTCF ChIP, not Hi-C." The same pattern repeats in hic_gate.json (net -0.003137298046080472, z -1.0554674798883492, sign_consistent false). Note also that chromatin_spheres.py's own distance control is bin-wise z-scoring, not a power law — even the file that produced the exponent did not consume it as a null.

(3) The shipped representation is unstable in two of its three numbers. The candidate proposes shipping measured -1.4053096461003798 alongside phantom -0.9605206529048974 and spheres -1.0956607241542549. Across the six recorded sphere runs, only `measured` is invariant — it is a property of the K562 Hi-C data, unchanged by every model knob, which is exactly why it is the one number worth keeping. The two simulated companions are knob artefacts: phantom moves 0.2531 (-0.9605206529048974 -> -0.7074) purely from CONTACT_R, and spheres spans 0.2805. Worse, the "self-avoidance steepens the decay 0.135 toward the data" claim that the candidate cites as proof the physics behaves correctly REVERSES at r_frac 0.95 / CONTACT_R 2.0, moving +0.1244 AWAY from the data — with available contact volume 1-(2*0.95/2)^3 = 0.143, the exact trap chromatin_spheres.py's docstring predicted. Shipping the phantom and sphere exponents "so the residual gap stays visible" ships a gap whose size is set by a scoring convention.

(4) Scope inflation. "One number per cell type" is 1 of 4 measured — only K562 has an exponent; the other three cell types in contact_decompose.json have loop coverage but no exponent. And the number is fit on 32 Mb of chr22, 1.0323% of the 3.1e9 bp genome.

WHERE MY ATTACK FAILED, and I concede it. I expected the known weak point — that the cell model holds no genomic coordinates — to kill this outright. It does not. cell_complete.json carries chrom and tss for 16380 of 16492 genes, and loops3d yields 960 cis gene-loop pairs with zero trans errors, median separation 230109 bp, and 92.3% landing inside the 50 kb-2 Mb window the exponent is fit over. The coordinate substrate is real and unusually well matched to the fit range. The residual coordinate gap is narrower and specific: `enh` is an integer count (0-245, sum 1456560), not positions, so enhancer-gene separation cannot be computed inside cell_complete.json — the coordinates that support the EG task live in crosscell_eg.py's CRISPR benchmark, which subsystem_links.json places in no subsystem at all, and which records missing_pairs [["4d chromatin","cell model"]]: zero code links, zero data links between exactly the two subsystems this coupling claims to join.

I also confirm the coupling needs no reduction that was measured to fail. It touches neither locality-by-norm (physics_reduce.json, FAILS at 1.0 vs threshold 0.25) nor finite-amplitude linearity (physics_reduce_rod.json, NOT TESTABLE). It is a data statistic, not a solve. That is why the verdict is REDUCED rather than BLOCKED: nothing physical forbids it, the measured value of the proposed use is simply indistinguishable from zero.

WHAT TO BUILD. Ship the certificate — "do not simulate the conformational ensemble at 25 kb" — with its three supporting deltas, which is the part carrying all the value (775 GPU-days). Ship exactly ONE float, measured -1.4053096461003798, labelled as what chromatin_spheres.py's own log calls it: "a theory check the correlation cannot give" — a K562/chr22 validation target that any future conformational model must reproduce, NOT a feature. Drop the phantom and sphere exponents from the interface (knob-dependent, one sign-flips). Drop "one number per cell type" (1 of 4 measured). Do not wire it into crosscell_eg/residual_contact scoring: the consumer already has log_dist, is a tree ensemble invariant to monotone transforms, and the stronger empirical version of this exact feature scored +0.0042193 MRR at sign_p 0.26014579678753663.

The certificate's saving, priced from chromatin_spheres.json's own log figure of ~1 GPU-day per region for the Langevin alternative at 4 Mb regions: 8 GPU-days over the recorded chr22 span (32 Mb), and 3.1e9/4e6 = 775 regions = 775 GPU-days genome-wide using the 3.1e9 bp genome from /home/user/cell/outputs/chromatin_cost_model.json. So the coupling is free and the refusal it carries is worth 775 GPU-days — but the exponent itself buys +0.0042193 MRR at sign_p 0.26014579678753663 (/home/user/cell/outputs/orphan/residual_contact.json), i.e. the saving is entirely in the certificate half, not the float half.
verdicts.refutation_attempted:
Strongest argument AGAINST: the exponent is informationally void in the consumer it names, and the repo has already measured that void. crosscell_eg.py carries log_dist as FEATNAMES[0] (X[i,0] = np.log10(max(abs(t-em),1))) plus dist_rank and dist_excess, and feeds them to xgboost; log P(s) = a*log s is an affine transform of an existing feature into a threshold-splitting tree ensemble that is invariant to monotone transforms, so a contributes exactly zero for any value. Independently, residual_contact.json built a STRICTLY STRONGER version of the same idea at the same 25000 bp resolution — per-distance-bin empirical expected, which its docstring says was chosen precisely "so no external expected-model is assumed" — and recorded +0.0010306 pooled, +0.0042193 MRR at dmrr_sign_p 0.26014579678753663, with the full contact block falling below baseline at 0.5548209174986355, verdict "NO".

Does it survive? YES, it survives, and it is what cuts the payload. I tried three counter-arguments and none rescued the exponent as a scoring input. (a) "Maybe the cell model lacks the coordinates so this is untestable rather than refuted" — false, the coordinates are there (16380/16492 genes with chrom+tss; 960 cis loop pairs, 92.3% inside the fit range), which makes the coupling testable and therefore refutable, and it was refuted. (b) "Maybe a parametric exponent generalises to cell types with no Hi-C where the empirical binning cannot be fit" — this is the one genuinely open line, but it is not measured anywhere in the repo: only K562 has an exponent, and contact_decompose.json's other three cell types have loop coverage without exponents, so the transfer claim has zero recorded support and cannot be credited. (c) "Maybe the value is in the theory check, not the score" — this one SURVIVES, and it is the reduced form I concede: the measured -1.4053096461003798 is invariant across all six sphere runs, so it is a legitimate validation target, exactly as chromatin_spheres.py labels it ("a theory check the correlation cannot give"). What does NOT survive alongside it are the phantom and sphere exponents, whose 0.2531 and 0.2805 knob-driven spreads and outright sign flip at r_frac 0.95 (+0.1244 away from the data, available contact volume 0.143) make "the residual gap stays visible" a statement about CONTACT_R rather than about chromatin.
verdicts.what_would_unblock: Three concrete, repo-shaped measurements would move this from BUILD REDUCED to BUILD NOW. (1) A non-tree, non-rank consumer. The invariance argument only bites because crosscell_eg.py feeds log_dist to xgboost. Re-run the residual_contact arms with a linear or explicitly parametric scorer where s^a is not absorbable, and record whether the exponent earns anything over the empirical per-bin expected already implemented — right now the empirical version dominates it by construction and scored +0.0042193 MRR at sign_p 0.26014579678753663. (2) Cross-cell-type transfer, which is the only place a one-parameter law can beat empirical binning. Fit the exponent on the K562 Hi-C already streamed and apply it to GM12878/HCT116/WTC11, which contact_decompose.json shows have loop coverage (0.7794117647058824 / 0.4797979797979798 / 0.4877667881311817) but no contact matrix; if a K562-fit exponent recovers a usable expected model where no matrix exists, the coupling has a job the empirical route cannot do. That test is not in the repo. (3) Knob stability for the simulated references. Re-run the R_FRAC x CONTACT_R grid at fixed available-contact-volume 1-(2r/c)^3 rather than fixed r, so the phantom-to-spheres shift can be reported without the r_frac 0.95 sign flip; until then the two simulated exponents must not ship. Separately, and cheaply: add enhancer POSITIONS (not just the 'enh' integer count, currently 0-245 summing to 1456560) to cell_complete.json, and create any code or data link across the 4d chromatin <-> cell model pair that subsystem_links.json currently records as the one missing pair — without that, this coupling has no wire to travel down regardless of whether the number is worth sending.

The candidate's individual citations all check out against the files -- I verified every one and found no fabricated number. schwarz_local really does sit at 0.9833069301764209 with last_change 0.0; two_level_modal really is 64 iterations at 4.11905669415648e-06; the coarse_only controls really do fail (4000 iters at 0.9392517024058951 and NaN), so the "preconditioner not reduced model" defence is sound and the 20% modal plateau does NOT bind. Genomic coordinates are not needed -- the basis is a property of one crystal structure, and the structure is in the container. So the usual killers all miss.

What kills it is a competitor inside the same repo, running on the same operator. chromatin_twolevel.py:188 builds K once from unmodified coordinates and injects every mark as a force vector (line 231-232), so K never changes across the 3.5e8 marks. That is precisely the regime chromatin_greens.py already priced: factorise once for 24.98612141609192 s, then 88.98566166559856 ms per right-hand side, independently confirmed by physics_reduce.json's "reusable factorisation" at 433.3280312231362x, HOLDS. It is 3.25x more expensive to set up AND 22.97x more expensive per mark, so it is dominated at every mark count -- there is no m at which it wins. And the coupling's own amortisation argument ("paid once for the family of 31M near-identical nucleosomes") applies verbatim to the factorisation, so the argument that is supposed to justify the coupling actually favours its competitor.

Three further defects in the pitch. (1) The failure being "fixed" is already fixed in the file that records it: nexus_methyl_propagate.json's schwarz_true_accelerated arm reaches 1.6388220255366465e-07 on the same 2898-sphere tiling, and that file's own log says "What repairs it is one global pass per sweep". nexus does not have a broken solve; it has a slow one. All 17 links are chromatin importing nexus (chromatin_twolevel.py:69-70 pulls elastic_network, exact_solve, build_spheres out of nexus_methyl_propagate). The proposed flow is an .npz produced by chromatin and consumed by nexus, and subsystem_links.json records ZERO data links from 4d chromatin to nexus -- the only data link in the whole file is cell model -> nexus via holdout_meta.json. Wiring the proposed direction as an import would close a cycle, since chromatin_modal.py already imports nexus_methyl_propagate. (3) The boundary being "crossed" is a filename rule: subsystem_links.py's SUB list assigns "nexus" to anything matching colab/nexus*, and nexus_methyl_propagate.py builds the identical 1KX5 network at the identical RC = 6.0 A. The repo contains exactly one structure (PDB_ID = "1KX5"). There is no recorded run of the 1KX5 basis on a second nucleosome: no sequence variant, no histone variant, no alternative conformation, no linker-length change. Note that the file's own predeclared fallback failed too -- the rigid-aggregate coarse space, which would have made the eigensolve unnecessary and structure-independent, was measured WORSE (151 and 99 iterations against 64 and 63), so the per-structure eigensolve cannot be avoided if the basis does not transfer.

verdicts.reasoning:
Three of the candidate's four factual pillars check out and I concede them: missing_pairs really is [['4d chromatin','cell model']]; the label really is computable for all 16,492 genes (I regenerated it in 14.7 s, 2,468 flagged); and the cell model really does hold genomic coordinates -- 16,380 of 16,492 records carry chrom and tss, so the expected weak point is not the weak point. The cost arithmetic also survives at 2 kb windows.

What does not survive is the mechanism, and it fails on a word. The cost model's HYSTERESIS is mechanical and topological in the rod's fine state -- 'a plectoneme pinned at a SEQUENCE FEATURE, a bubble that stays open' -- living on tau(200 bp) = 87 ns against tau(10 kb) = 219 us. The epigenetics module's hysteresis is read-write chemical feedback on histone marks propagating across cell generations ('losing one writer often does nothing -- surviving marks re-propagate'). Two different physical quantities sharing one English word. The candidate's central claim, that two subsystems arrived at the same failure mode from opposite ends, is the pun, not a measurement.

Test the pun against the repo. The only recorded experiment that asks whether a chemical mark propagates into rod-scale fine structure is chromatin_twist_energy, and it FAILS its shuffled control: 0.0026 deg at 40-80 bp against 0.1824 deg shuffled, with the control 70.2x larger. Its companion result -- interface strain ratio 0.0070 for 5mC against 1.51 shuffled -- carries an explicit instruction not to assume the bridge downstream. That is precisely the assumption this coupling makes.

Worse, the target quantity does not exist on the physics side at all. Nothing in this repo measures a pinned plectoneme or a persistent bubble. chromatin_supercoil.json is equilibrium Metropolis MC on a homogeneous 3600 bp circle with uniform C and no sequence; a memoryless sampler cannot produce history dependence, so the mask cannot be validated or refuted there. Its one quantitative gate already failed in the fatal direction (writhe_fraction false, 0.9657 vs 0.70-0.75), which under-estimates torque -- and torque is what drives melting and pinning. chromatin_partition_probes and chromatin_resolution both tried and failed to close that gap.

The consumer is also absent. refine() in chromatin_rod.py splits EVERY segment; there is no masked refinement, no moving boundary, no MTS implementation. The 4.44e-16 Lk drift that licenses the whole 1.2 min/Mb story is eight whole-chain operations -- exactly not the mixed-resolution boundary the cost model flags as the engineering risk. So the mask would be handed to a closed-form spreadsheet expression, not a scheduler.

Finally the label itself is weaker than quoted. The cited 4.07 enrichment and 1.084 vs -1.0 split are bivalent-only (n=220). The polycomb_repressed class -- 1,754 of 2,468 loci, 71% of the mask -- has median log10 RPKM 0.371 and frac_expressed 0.582, statistically indistinguishable from quiescent and primed_weak, with H3K27me3 discriminating silence at AUC 0.571. Per the repo's own doctrine that rejections are the deliverable: a coupling whose bridging measurement lost to its shuffled control, whose target quantity is unmeasured, and whose consumer is unimplemented is BLOCKED, not BUILD REDUCED. The reduced form worth having is not this coupling -- it is the join table plus the physics-side hysteresis experiment that would make the coupling testable.

verdicts.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and it broke in three places, two of which are fatal.

FIRST, the bridge it proposes to export is wrong, and I measured it rather than inferring it. The candidate is right that colab/chromatin_twist_energy.py already builds a base-pair index and that outputs/orphan/chromatin_twist_energy.json records n_pairs=84. I ran that module's own base_pairs() against the repo's 1kx5.pdb and reproduced 84 exactly. But 1KX5 has 147 C1' atoms in each DNA chain, and the canonical anti-parallel pairing A[i]<->B[146-i] gives C1'–C1' distances of 9.996–11.357 Å — all 147 inside the module's own 8.0–13.0 Å acceptance window. So the structure supports a complete 147/147 index and the algorithm throws away 43% of it. Worse: of the 84 it does return, 81 (96.4%) are mispaired by +1 to +3 bp, and the offset histogram {+1:52, +2:23, +3:5, -1:1, 0:3} is one-directional, so it would not average out. The cause is the module's documented design choice — "Geometry, not residue numbering, because the numbering convention of a PDB is not something to depend on" — which fails because nucleosomal DNA is bent and a neighbouring base's C1' is often marginally closer, after which the greedy `used` set cascades the error (43 of the 63 drops are collisions, not distance failures). I checked the symmetric fix too: mutual-nearest-neighbour resolves only 49/147, all 49 mispaired. Pure geometry does not work on this structure. The candidate proposes to ship this table with `resolved (bool — 84 of ~147 are True today)`, i.e. to export the 84 as ground truth. An index that is 96.4% off-register is not a shared coordinate system; it is a silent frame-shift injected at the base of every future coupling, and being off by 1–3 bp is the worst possible error size because it is small enough to look like physics.

SECOND, and decisively, the genomic half cannot be built. The coupling is defined as "the map from a genomic base pair to the atom indices". Closing that requires phase_offset_bp, and there is no nucleosome-positioning data in this container. I listed outputs/orphan/invivo/marks/ (dnase, h3k27ac, h3k27me3, h3k4me1, h3k4me3, h3k9me3, polr2a, polr2s5, procap_bi, abc_all.bedpe.gz) and grepped the whole repo: the only "MNase-seq" string anywhere is an ENCODE portal assay-title catalogue in outputs/orphan/translation.json — a list of what exists at ENCODE, not downloaded data. The candidate flags this itself under NOT MEASURED, and it is the correct call, but it is not a caveat on the coupling — it is the coupling. Without it you have an intra-nucleosome atom index, which is an internal 4d-chromatin bookkeeping artifact, not a link to the cell model.

THIRD, two of the three stated motivations do not survive checking. (a) "An atom index means different things in different runs today, so any coupling that ships bare atom integers is already broken." I diagnosed the 13607/13625 split: the difference is exactly 18 atoms = 14 MN + 4 CL ions, and they occupy array positions 13607–13624, i.e. all trailing. The two conventions agree atom-for-atom on every index below 13607, and the shift at all three recorded mark sites (5093, 9037, 6868) is 0. It is an append, not a re-index. That motivation is refuted. (b) "4d chromatin reads zero files" — subsystem_map.json does show before_datasets=[] and after_datasets=[], but the same file shows ran_clean=3 of 14 modules with 10 recorded as "TIMEOUT after 240s". The empty dataset lists are a tracer artifact; the modules demonstrably read 1kx5.pdb (I parsed 16755 atoms through their own loader). Only the third motivation stands: missing_pairs = [['4d chromatin','cell model']] is genuinely recorded in subsystem_links.json.

I also checked the cell-model side, which the brief flags as a known weak point, and found it is actually STRONGER than the candidate claims — which paradoxically makes the case worse. cell_complete.json carries not just chrom/tss on 16380 of 16492 genes but also a `loops3d` block with 767 entries. So the cell model does hold genomic coordinates. But its native resolution is kilobases ("3:138640kb"), colab/chromatin_spheres.py line 68 pins RES = 25_000, and the finest bead priced anywhere in chromatin_cost_model.json is 200 bp. The registry resolves 1 bp. There is no consumer on the cell-model side within 200x of the registry's granularity, and 25,000x at the Hi-C resolution actually used. The candidate confirmed one real defect I should credit: `tss` is a string in 16492/16492 records and there is no assembly field anywhere (hg38/GRCh38/hg19/GRCh37 all occur 0 times; the 2697 hits on "assembly" are GO text like "protein-containing complex assembly"), while chromatin_spheres.py says hg38 and cellos.py says GRCh38. That agreement is genuinely implicit and unenforced.

Finally, the registry has nothing to carry. Every payload channel measured in this repo is dead: interface strain, the proposed accessibility route, gives a 5mC enrichment ratio of 0.00704 against a shuffled control at 1.5136 — the random control loads the DNA–histone grip 215.1x more than the real mark, and chromatin_twist_energy.json states outright that the accessibility bridge "is NOT supported by this evidence and should not be assumed downstream". Twist at range gives 5mC 0.00054 deg at 20–40 bp against the shuffled control's 0.26168, a control 484.6x larger. And locality by norm FAILS in physics_reduce.json at quantity 1.0 versus threshold 0.25, with no radius to 100 Å reaching 90% of the norm. So even a perfect registry would connect a working atomistic solver to a cell model via three channels that have each been measured not to exist.

Cost is affordable — 0.044 s, ~9.3e-6 of the smallest job priced in the repo. That is precisely the trap: the arithmetic says yes and the evidence says no. Default is BLOCKED when repo evidence does not show it works, and here the repo evidence actively shows the proposed artifact is mispaired at 96.4% and its second table has no data source.
verdicts.refutation_attempted:
The strongest argument AGAINST this coupling is the one I built and it holds: the artifact proposed for export is measurably wrong (81/84 = 96.4% of its own resolved rows are off-register by +1 to +3 bp, against a canonical pairing whose 147/147 C1'–C1' distances all fall inside the module's own 8.0–13.0 Å window), and its genomic half has no data source in this container (no MNase track; the sole "MNase-seq" string in the repo is an ENCODE portal catalogue entry in outputs/orphan/translation.json).

I stress-tested this against the best pro-coupling rebuttals, and report where it costs me ground.

Rebuttal 1, the strongest: "This is an ADAPTER, not a payload. A precondition does not need a working consumer — you build the coordinate system first and the physics later, so dead payload channels are irrelevant." This is architecturally legitimate and I concede it partially. It does NOT rescue the coupling, for two independent reasons. A precondition that is itself 96.4% wrong is not a precondition, it is a frame-shift bug propagated to everything built on top, and a 1–3 bp systematic offset is the worst error magnitude because it is too small to crash and too large to ignore. And the adapter argument cannot conjure phase_offset_bp: table 1 is intra-nucleosome bookkeeping, table 2 is the actual bridge, and table 2 has no input.

Rebuttal 2: "The pairing bug is one line — you measured the fix yourself (147/147 canonical, distance-validated, in 0.0022 s). Fix it and build." This one genuinely costs me ground and is why my what_would_unblock is short and concrete rather than a wall. But the fix requires abandoning the module's explicit, documented design principle ("Geometry, not residue numbering..."), and my measurement shows that principle is the error's source — symmetric mutual-nearest-neighbour, the obvious geometric repair, resolves only 49/147 with all 49 mispaired. So the correct method is the one the file deliberately rejected, which means this is a design reversal requiring re-validation of the twist results built on the 84 pairs, not a one-line patch. And it still leaves the coupling blocked at table 2.

Rebuttal 3: "Genome-wide phasing is optional — pin one nucleosome to one locus by hand and demonstrate the join." Survives as a demo, fails as a coupling: one hand-placed nucleosome is 147 bp against 15.5 M nucleosomes genome-wide (chromatin_cost_model.json), and nothing on the cell-model side reads below 200 bp/bead (finest AMR level) or 25 kb (chromatin_spheres.py RES).

Where the candidate beat me: its cell-model-side critique is correct and I verified every part of it — tss really is a string in 16492/16492 records, and there really is no assembly field (hg38/GRCh38/hg19/GRCh37 = 0 occurrences) while chromatin_spheres.py line 65 says hg38 and cellos.py says GRCh38. Making assembly an explicit column is right. I also found supporting evidence the candidate missed: mark site 6868 is labelled "phospho-S" but is OG1 of a THREONINE in chain A, which is exactly the atom-index-to-biological-identity drift the registry is meant to prevent. That strengthens the motivation while doing nothing for the feasibility.

Where I beat the candidate: the 13607-vs-13625 argument, presented as forcing resolution of "a live representation bug", is refuted — the 18 atoms are 14 MN + 4 CL at trailing positions 13607–13624, and the index shift is 0 at all three recorded mark sites. And "4d chromatin reads zero files" is a tracer artifact: 10 of 14 modules recorded TIMEOUT after 240s in subsystem_map.json.
verdicts.what_would_unblock:
Three things, in order. Only the first is free.

(1) FIX THE PAIRING BEFORE EXPORTING ANYTHING. Replace the greedy geometric match in colab/chromatin_twist_energy.py base_pairs() (source line 83 region) with residue-order registration validated by distance: pair A[i]<->B[146-i] and assert 8.0 < d < 13.0. Measured: this yields 147/147 with every distance in 9.996–11.357 Å, in 0.0022 s. Do NOT use symmetric mutual-nearest-neighbour — I measured it at 49/147, all mispaired. Ship nuc_bp_atom_map.tsv with 147 rows, not the proposed 84. Add a regression assertion that the resolved count is 147 and that every offset j-(146-i) is 0, so the frame-shift cannot silently return.

(2) RE-VALIDATE WHAT WAS BUILT ON THE BROKEN INDEX. The twist-vs-sequence-separation results in outputs/orphan/chromatin_twist_energy.json are binned in base pairs using these 84 pairs, and 81 of them are off-register by 1–3 bp. The bins are 0–2, 2–5, 5–10, 10–20, 20–40, 40–80 bp, so a systematic +1 to +3 shift is comparable to the width of the three narrowest bins. That result already fails against its shuffled control (5mC 0.00054 deg vs shuffled 0.26168 at 20–40 bp), so the conclusion is unlikely to move, but the number should be regenerated on the corrected index before anyone cites the bp axis.

(3) GET NUCLEOSOME POSITIONING DATA, or the coupling stays blocked regardless of (1) and (2). phase_offset_bp needs an MNase-seq or chemical-cleavage nucleosome map for K562 to match the existing Hi-C and ChIP (outputs/orphan/invivo/manifest.json: chrom chr22, cell K562). ENCODE lists MNase-seq among K562 assays — that string is already in outputs/orphan/translation.json — so the dataset exists upstream; it is simply not in this container. Until it is on disk, genomic_bp -> atom_index cannot be evaluated, only asserted.

Also required before the join means anything, and cheap: add an explicit `assembly` column to both TSVs and backfill cell_complete.json's gene records, since it currently has no assembly field at all; and cast `tss` from string to int (16492/16492 are strings today).

Worth stating plainly: completing all of the above yields a correct registry that still has nothing measured to carry across it. Interface strain enrichment is 0.00704 for 5mC against 1.5136 for a shuffled control (215.1x the wrong way), twist does not beat its shuffled control at range, and locality by norm FAILS at 1.0 vs threshold 0.25. So the honest sequencing is to first identify one channel with a measured, control-beating signal, and let that channel dictate the registry's required resolution — rather than build a 1 bp index for consumers whose finest object is 200 bp and whose working resolution is 25 kb.

verdicts.reasoning: I could not refute this on cost, and I tried. Every descriptive number in the proposal is real: I recounted all nine peak files and got the candidate's counts to the peak, confirmed 254000.0 nucleosomes and the 592x sparsity ratio, and reproduced 4290 x 0.11661982536315918 = 500.3 core-s. Cost is not the constraint by any route — the exact full-structure route is 24.986 s factorisation plus 0.089 s per column (chromatin_greens.json), so even 4290 independent columns is 406.7 core-s. The coupling fails on two other things instead. FIRST, the peak list does not fit the measured force models. Only three force models were ever characterised — steric (5mC), charge +1->0 (acetyl-K), charge 0->-2 (phospho-S). Of the five marks in the representation, four are lysine methylation, which the source file itself classifies as "sterically like 5mC", and the steric channel is the one measured never to converge (0.3496 at 40 A, "region needed: 5mC None"). That is 3441 of 4290 peaks, 80.21%. The candidate anticipated this constraint for 5mC/CpG and then walked its own peak list straight into it. Meanwhile the only channel that converges at the 20 A radius its cost estimate uses is phospho-S screened, and there is no phospho track in the container. So exactly one of the five marks — h3k27ac, 849 peaks, 19.79% — has both data and a measured-convergent force model. SECOND, and worse, the coupling transmits no information. Its stated purpose is "replacing the arbitrary hardcoded atom index", but it cannot supply an atom index. The solver runs on one fixed 1KX5 structure fetched by ID; there is no nucleosome positioning data anywhere in the container (no MNase or dyad file, and grep over colab/ finds no mention of either), so nuc_offset_bp cannot be computed, and no code path builds a sequence-specific nucleosome. The force is a function of (atom index, charge delta) alone. Every h3k27ac peak on chr22 therefore produces the identical displacement field: 849 rows, one distinct value. Genomic coordinate in, zero bits through. "Per-locus mechanical strain" is not per-locus — it is per-chemistry, and the peak list contributes only a multiplicity count. THIRD, even the surviving 19.79% is an extrapolation off its measurement. The 40 A convergence for acetyl was measured at atom 9037, LYS NZ on chain D — I checked the chain lengths in the cached PDB and chain D is 122 residues, i.e. H2B, not H3 — and the docstring says sites were "chosen as the most buried of each type". H3K27ac sits on an exposed H3 N-terminal tail. The file's own explanation of why convergence happens is the ratio of local response to the whole-particle breathing floor; a weakly-packed tail site pushes that ratio toward the 5mC failure mode. Convergence at H3K27 is unmeasured and the one measured data point argues the pessimistic way. FOURTH, the promised output has no measured destination. The artefact is per-locus strain, and chromatin_twist_energy.json measured interface loading at 0.01x and 0.00x its share of springs against 1.51x for a shuffled control, concluding in the file itself that the accessibility bridge "should not be assumed downstream". Strain distributes with network connectivity, not with the DNA-histone grip, so there is no measured channel carrying this back to the cell model. I land on BUILD REDUCED rather than BLOCKED only because a genuinely buildable remnant exists with measured support: h3k27ac against the acetyl-K charge +1->0 channel, convergent at 40 A to 0.0354. But the reduced form is a precomputed lookup table of at most 5 full-structure fields keyed on (chain, resid, force_model), computed once for 25.4 core-s via the Green route, and joined to the 849 peaks as an ANNOTATION. It is not a per-locus solve, it produces no per-locus variation, and it must not be reported as a genomic coupling. Note also that the local-region route is the wrong route regardless: doing the full-structure solve makes the region radius irrelevant and sidesteps the 5mC non-convergence entirely, at lower cost than the 40 A region sweep.
